prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Labour Party Manifesto 2019 – Summary (≤500 words)

Vision and funding
- “Real change” for the many: rebalance wealth and power; end austerity; decarbonise fast.
- £400bn National Transformation Fund (incl. £250bn Green Transformation Fund); National & Regional Investment Banks; local transformation funds; decentralisation of power.

Green Industrial Revolution
- Aim for most emissions cuts by 2030; 1m climate jobs; net‑zero trajectory in 2030s.
- Massive renewables build (offshore/onshore wind, solar), new nuclear; trial tidal; ban fracking.
- Retrofit almost all 27m homes; heat pumps/district heat/hydrogen; smarter grid/storage.
- Windfall tax on oil; public stakes in green generation; public ownership of energy and water with new national/regional energy agencies.

Transport
- Rail and buses into public ownership; reinstate routes; free bus travel for under‑25s where councils run buses.
- Rail electrification, HS2 to Scotland, Crossrail North; boost freight; cycling/walking plans; Vision Zero.
- Target 2030 for ending new ICE car sales; EV infrastructure and public fleet transition.

Environment and food
- Clean Air Act; stronger flood defences; tree planting; expand protected areas; restore nature.
- Producer responsibility for waste; bottle return; plastics remanufacturing; strong animal welfare.
- Right to Food; halve food bank use in a year, end need in three; support sustainable farming/fishing.

Economy, work and tax
- Rewrite company rules for long‑termism; worker directors (1/3); tougher takeover and audit rules.
- Real Living Wage £10; end zero‑hours; day‑one rights; sectoral bargaining; stronger unions.
- Move towards 32‑hour average week in a decade with no loss of pay.
- Fairer taxes: higher income tax >£80k; partial reversal of corporation tax cuts; no VAT rise; clamp down on avoidance; presumption to insource; end PFI; public sector pay rises (5% first year).

Public services
- NHS: 4.3% avg annual funding rise; end/reverse privatisation; more scanners/AI/IT; free prescriptions and basic dentistry; net‑zero NHS; major mental health investment and children’s hubs.
- Social care: National Care Service; free personal care; cap costs; better pay/conditions for carers.
- Education: National Education Service; restore/expand Sure Start; 30hrs free preschool for 2–4s; extend maternity leave to 12 months; scrap KS1/2 SATs; arts premium; bring academies/free schools under local control; free school meals for all primaries; lifelong learning entitlements; abolish tuition fees and restore maintenance grants.

Housing
- Build >1m social homes in a decade (100k/yr council homes); end Right to Buy; redefine “affordable” to local incomes; standards upgrade.
- Private renting: rent caps tied to inflation (with local powers), open‑ended tenancies, national licensing and enforcement; end no‑fault evictions; fix leasehold abuses.
- Grenfell response: £1bn for sprinklers/safety; replace dangerous cladding. End rough sleeping in 5 years.

Justice, policing and rights
- Recruit more officers/PCSOs/staff; rebuild neighbourhood policing; victims’ standards.
- Reunify probation; restore legal aid; presumption against short prison terms; tackle VAWG; inquiries into historic injustices.
- Digital: free full‑fibre broadband via publicly owned British Broadband; digital rights and online safety.

Migration and social security
- End “hostile environment”; scrap 2014 Act; end indefinite detention; safe, legal routes for refugees; equal work rights.
- Scrap Universal Credit; end five‑week wait/sanctions; scrap benefit cap and two‑child limit; raise LHA; disability assessments in‑house; stronger support for disabled people and carers.
- Pensions: keep triple lock; WASPI redress; fair schemes; single public dashboard.

Constitution and democracy
- Abolish Lords for an elected Senate after a constitutional convention; votes at 16; automatic voter registration; curb dark money/lobbying; extend FOI.

Brexit
- Final‑say referendum within six months: choice between a new soft‑Brexit deal (customs union, close Single Market alignment, rights and standards guarantees) and Remain; implement result.

Foreign policy and defence
- Human‑rights‑led diplomacy; War Powers Act; suspend arms sales linked to abuses; recognise Palestine; rebuild climate diplomacy.
- Maintain NATO, 2% of GDP defence spend, renew Trident; improve forces’ pay, housing and veteran support.

International development
- Keep DfID and 0.7% aid; climate justice focus; end fossil‑fuel aid/finance; fair trade, tax and medicines access.
